judge.rationale: All six words share the 'hydro'/'hydr' root chain (hydroxidion-hydroxide-hydroxyl-hydrocarbon-hydrogen-hydrate), forming one connected group of shared-stem chemical terms; the gap's adverb requirement is not reflected in these noun-form candidates so no inflection stripping applies.
The only overlap, 'dick'/'prick' sharing 'ick', is an accidental letter run with no shared root and no chain to any other candidate, so no usable group exists.

Polarization and polarisation are the same word differing only by British/American -z-/-s- spelling, an orthographic variant, while conductivity/conductance share only a stem plus distinct noun-forming suffixes and form a separate, non-linked pair.
No pair of these words shares any substring of three or more characters, so there is no basis for a shape-based group.
refolution is a period spelling variant of resolution, and resolve shares the resol- stem with both, forming a chain distinct from the merely suffix-based -ion/-tion overlaps among the other nouns.
No pair of candidates shares any substring of three or more characters, so there is no shared-shape group to report.
appall, appeared, and appear all share the initial stem 'app-', with appeared and appear sharing the fuller root 'appear', chaining them into one group via appall's 'app' overlap.
The two overlaps ('ion' shared as a common noun-forming suffix, and 'ran' as an accidental cross-word letter run) do not reflect shared roots, so no genuine form group links any of these words.

All nine words share the Latin prefix sub- combined with variant stems (subvers-, subvert-, subiect-/subject-) that chain together through overlapping substrings, forming one connected root-based group while 'sub' alone links in only via the bare prefix.

Molecule and molecular share the root 'molecul-' with different endings, while the other pairs (neutron/neutral, positive/negative, corpuscle/nucleus) are isolated two-word overlaps that don't chain into a larger connected group.
No pair among these words shares any substring of three or more characters, so there is no shape-based group to report.
lysogenic and lysogenesis share the root lysogen-, while phagocytosis, positive, and lysogenesis only overlap by short accidental substrings (sis, osi) that do not form a real shared root chain.
The overlap table shows no pair of candidates sharing a substring of three or more characters, so no form group can be constructed.
No pair of these ten words shares a substring of three or more characters, so no shape-based group can be formed.
All seven words chain together through the shared 'hydro' root, with tighter overlaps (hydrox-, hydroxyl-) nesting within that larger shared stem.
No pair of these short function words shares any substring of three or more characters, so there is no usable shape-based group.
culture and cultivation share the root 'cult', while the other overlaps (tion/ation/ion/sis) are just noun-forming suffixes shared across unrelated roots, not stem material.

The only overlap (antigens/sensitizers sharing 'ens') is an accidental substring, not a shared root, and the rest of the candidates are plural nouns whose shared -s ending is simply the grammar the gap requires.
Brother, mother, and father chain together through shared endings 'other'/'ther', a kinship-noun suffix pattern rather than grammatical inflection, while fodder/mudder form a separate unlinked pair.

The '-tion/-ion' overlaps across position, version, interpretation, explanation are just the common noun-forming suffix required by the slot, not a shared root, leaving only explanation/explanations as a genuine same-lemma pair.
